If the item allows its user to cast any spells from it, you must craft the item yourself (the facility’s hirelings can assist), and you must have all those spells prepared every day you spend crafting the item.
Storehouse
Level 5 Bastion Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Trade

A Storehouse is a cool, dark space meant to contain trade goods objects from the Trade Goods table in chapter 7 and from chapter 6 of the Player’s Handbook.
Trade: Goods. When you issue the Trade order to this facility, its hireling spends the next 7 days procuring nonmagical items that have a total value of 500 GP or less and stores them in the Storehouse, or the hireling uses those 7 days to sell goods in the Storehouse. You bear the total cost of any purchases, and the maximum value of the items purchased increases to 2,000 GP when you reach level 9 and 5,000 GP when you reach level 13.
When you sell goods from your Storehouse, the buyer pays you 10 percent more than the standard price; this profit increases to 20 percent when you reach level 9, 50 percent when you reach level 13, and 100 percent when you reach level 17.
Trapworks
Level 5 Bastion Facility

Prerequisite: Proficiency with Thieves’ Tools or Sleight of Hand
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Craft

A Trapworks is a foundry of morbid creativity. Disarmed and reassembled contraptions are sprawled across the floor and built into the walls as you work towards your own new Designs.
Steady Hands. After spending a long rest in your bastion, you gain Advantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks made to disarm traps over the next 7 days.
Craft Options. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, choose one of thefollowing options:
Craft: Portable Trap. You commission your hireling to create a multipurpose portable trap that you’ve designed. The creation of it takes 7 days and costs 50 gold. You can only have one portable trap at a time. If a new portable trap is crafted, the old one stops loses its functionality.
These traps can be set using just the utilize action and you can choose both the effect and the mode of activation each time you use the item. The portable trap can be used up to 4 times but each effect and mode of activation can only be used once. The save DC for these effects is 8 plus your proficiency bonus plus your dexterity modifier.

























Mode of ActivationDescriptionTrip WireYou run a line of thin wire 30ft across any surface.The trap activates when a creature moves throughthat area and the effect is centered on thatcreature and in the direction the creature camefrom if applicable.DecoyYou disguise the trap to look like a full coin purseor something valuable. The trap activates when acreature interacts with it and the effect is centeredon that creature and in the direction the creaturecame from if applicable.Remote TriggerYou set up a pull pin attached to a run of string thatyou can pull to activate the trap with your reaction.You decide where the effect will be placed whenyou set the trap.TimerYou set a timer to activate the trap that runsbetween 6 seconds and 10 minutes. You decidewhere the effect will be placed when you set thetrap.

























Trap EffectDescriptionPit TrapCreatures within 15ft must make a dexterity savingthrow or fall 30ft into a magical pit as they landprone and take 3d6 bludgeoning damage.Poison SprayCreatures within 20ft must make a constitutionsaving throw or take 2d10 poison damage andgain the poisoned condition for 1 minute.Fire GoutCreatures within a 30ft cone must make a dexteritysaving throw or take 2d10 fire damage and beginburning.ShrapnelCreatures within 20ft must make a dexterity savingthrow or take 3d10 piercing damage.
Workshop
Level 5 Bastion Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 3
Order: Craft

This Workshop is a creative space where useful items can be crafted.
Artisan’s Tools. The Workshop comes equipped with six different kinds of Artisan’s Tools, chosen from the following list:

Carpenter’s Tools
Cobbler’s Tools
Glassblower’s Tools
Jeweler’s Tools
Leatherworker’s Tools
Mason’s Tools
Painter’s Tools
Potter’s Tools
Tinker’s Tools
Weaver’s Tools
Woodcarver’s Tools

Craft Options. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, choose one of the following options:
Craft: Adventuring Gear. The facility’s hirelings craft anything that can be made with the tools you chose when you added the Workshop to your Bastion (see above), using the rules in the Player’s Handbook.
Craft: Magic Item (Implement). If you are level 9+, you can commission the facility’s hirelings to craft a Common or an Uncommon magic item chosen by you from the Implements tables in chapter 7. The facility has the tool required to craft the item, and the hirelings have proficiency with that tool as well as proficiency in the Arcana skill. See the “Crafting Magic Items” section in chapter 7 for the time and money that must be spent to craft the item. If the item allows its user to cast any spells from it, you must craft the item yourself (the facility’s hirelings can assist), and you must have all those spells prepared every day you spend crafting the item.
Source of Inspiration. After spending an entire Short Rest in your Workshop, you gain Heroic Inspiration. You can’t gain this benefit again until you finish a Long Rest.
Enlarging the Facility. You can enlarge your Workshop to a Vast facility by spending 2,000 GP. If you do so, the Workshop gains two additional hirelings and three additional Artisan’s Tools (chosen from the list above).

Faction Facilities
Nevercough Tribunal
Case Law Archives
Level 5 Azorius Senate (Nevercough Tribunal) Facility

Prerequisite: Rank 2 Renown with Azorius Senate
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Research

The Case Law Archives is a small room riddled with shelves inlaid into the walls, and laden with chests with scrolls, tomes, and books copied from the guild archives themselves. This room is meticulously organized and smells of parchment, candle wax and ink. Your hirelings spend the majority of their days sifting through pages, reading and studying, deliberating and discussing the events of the Senate’s innumerable cases.
Research: Unique Information. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you may gain pertinent information about the surrounding community, guilds in the area or information about resolved and unresolved cases around your Bastion. Choose one; Insight, Investigation or Perception. You gain Advantage on any D20 Tests that use your chosen skill; while operating near your Bastion, once Advantage is spent, another Research order must be given before you may receive this bonus again.
Chamber Of Precognition
Level 5 Azorius Senate (Nevercough Tribunal) Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use an Arcane Focus or a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Empower

One of the Azorius Senate’s foundational yet niche law enforcement chamber designs. Quaint
and rather plain amongst the rest of the guild architecture. You have been provided 2 precognitive
Mages for your Bastion due to your station within the guild. Your mages understand your core
mission is to mete out justice and bring order to the anarchistic ways of the other guilds. Your mages offer you a portent of knowledge.
Empower: Stay Vigilant. When you use the Empower Action on this facility, you and your party are
granted the ability to cast the spell Portent (Players Guide Pg117) without expending a spell slot, you may cast this up to 1D4 times. The cost is 250 GP, and the ritual takes 2 days to complete.
Deputy Barracks
Level 5 Azorius Senate (Nevercough Tribunal) Facility

Prerequisite: Renown Rank of 2 or higher with the Azorius Senate
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Recruit

The Deputy Barracks design represents the Azorius Senate’s staunch adherence to practicality and
order, a plain yet functional room with bunks for your assigned deputies and enforcers. The Senate
has provided you and your hirelings the opportunity to work with other diligent enforcers of the Senate’s order, while the Senate has provided you two enforcers (Pick two: Lawmages / Justiciar / Officer) These enforcers operate as your deputies and can assist in your investigations, interrogations, and keeping of the peace.
Recruit: Bastion Defenders. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you may recruit up to
4 additional Arrestor (see Arrestor below) to stand ever vigil for your Bastion and its surrounding
community. This action has no monetary cost, however, your recruits will return to their previous
postings at the end of your next Bastion turn.
Arrestor
Medium Humanoid (any Species), Any Alignment
Armor Class 17 (Splint)
Hit Points 60 (9D8+19)
Speed 30 ft.





















STRDEXCONINTWISCHA17 (+3)12 (+1)14 (+2)10 (+0)11 (+0)15 (+2)
Saving Throws Con +4, Wis +2
Senses passive Perception 20
Languages Any Two Languages(Usually Common)
Challenge 2 (450 XP)
—Actions
Multiattack. The Arrestor makes two melee attacks or one spell attack
Longsword. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: (1d10) Piercing damage.
—Spells Known
At Will: Sacred Flame
—Reactions
Shield Bash. When the Arrestor takes damage from one melee attack and presses into the fray lunging with their shield in a wide arc, dealing 1d8 damage on a successful hit, To do so, the
Arrestor must see the attacker and be wielding a shield.
Hall Of Lawmages
Level 5 Azorius Senate (Nevercough Tribunal) Facility
Prerequisite: Renown Rank of 1 or higher with the Azorius Senate
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Empower
The Hall of Lawmages is a respected and almost traditional hall for any guild building, these halls
regardless of size and grandeur are places of wisdom and information.
Empower: Orderly Respite. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you may take the
effects of a Long Rest in half the amount of time.
Holding Cells
Level 5 Azorius Senate (Nevercough Tribunal) Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 4
Order: Empower/Recruit/Research

The Holding Cells are a crucial feature of the Azorius Senate’s outlying facilities, a sturdy unadorned room with several cells to hold persons of interest, whether they are suspects, criminals or individuals needing Senate protection. The Senate has granted special privileges to their enforcers who implement these facilities. Due to the increasingly unstable times these cells serve multiple purposes.
Facility Options: You may choose one of the following orders for this facility.
Empower: Eyes Of The Senate. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you temporarily gain the Alert Feat for 1d10 days. Information extracted from prisoners provides you with more than you could have hoped for.
Recruit: Oathsworn. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you can recruit up to four
new Bastion Defenders to fill the ranks of your Bastion. You can choose a combination of Defenders from Oathsworn (see Oathsworn below), Arrestor (see Arrestor above). This recruitment incurs no monetary cost, these Defenders have been given a second chance to serve society by swearing an oath to the Azorius Senate.
Research: Streetwise Information. When you issue the Research order to this facility, gain Advantage on your next Tactical Bastion turn.
Oathsworn
Medium Humanoid (any Species), Any Alignment
Armor Class 16 (Chain)
Hit Points 48 (5D8+8)
Speed 30 ft.





















STRDEXCONINTWISCHA17 (+3)12 (+1)12 (+1)10 (+0)11 (+0)13 (+1)
Saving Throws Con +2, Wis +2
Senses passive Perception 20
Languages Any Two Languages (Usually Common)
Challenge 2 (400 XP)
Second Chance. The Oathsworn are determined to turn their life around, having sworn an oath to the Azorius senate they rally their determination and have Advantage on saving throws against
the Frightened condition.
—Actions
Multiattack. The Arrestor makes two melee attacks or one spell attack
Longsword. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: (1d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: (1d10) piercing damage.
—Reactions
Shield Bash. When the Oathsworn takes damage from one
melee attack and presses into the fray lunging with their shield in
a wide arc, dealing 1d8 damage on a successful hit, To do so, the
Oathsworn must see the attacker and be wielding a shield
Reflecting Pools
Level 5 Azorius Senate Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use a Holy Symbol or Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Harvest

The Reflecting Pools are a common site within guild courts and buildings, keeping law and order is no calming ordeal. These pools are tended to carefully and lined with bushes, shrubs and trees that bear fruit. The pools often have a small fountain with which you can fill a small cup or chalice and imbibe the refreshing waters.
Harvest: Reflective Serenity. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, you can gather 3 vials
of Healing Potion or 15 bushels of fruit (worth 5 GP each). The harvesting process takes 7 days and
incurs no monetary cost. The fruit has the same effect as the Goodberry spell but does not expire in 24 hours. If not consumed they expire at the start of your next Bastion turn.
Scribes Study
Level 5 Azorius Senate Facility

Prerequisite: Renown Rank of 1 or higher with the Azorius Senate
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 4
Order: Craft

The scribe study is a common room, ordained with simple room dividers separating sleeping quarters with well-maintained ornate desks. Here you house several of the Senate’s recruits allowing them to experience the lawlessness at the fringes of guild territory. These scribes study law and Senate history. They’ve also been directed to aid you as they are permitted at their current station.
Craft: Guild Spells. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, your scribes can provide you with 1d4 spell scrolls. With your choice of spells, Command, Hold Person, Ensnaring Strike. The cost is 50 GP per scroll, and crafting time is 7 days.
Tribunal Highblade Coalition
Garden of the Dawn’s Radiance
Level 5 Boros Legion Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use a Holy Symbol or Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Harvest

The Garden of the Dawn’s Radiance is a vibrant space filled with flora that embodies healing and rejuvenation. Blossoming flowers and healing herbs thrive here, tended to by skilled gardeners who
understand the ways of nature and the divine.
Harvest: Bountiful Blossoms. When you issue the
Harvest order to this facility, you can gather ten vials of Healing Potion or ten exquisite floral bouquets (worth 5 GP each). The harvesting process takes 7 days and incurs no monetary cost.
Garrison Barracks
Level 5 Boros Legion Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Recruit

The Garrison Barracks serves as the primary living quarters for the Bastion’s Defenders. Furnished with beds, storage for gear, and communal areas, this facility fosters camaraderie and readiness among those who serve the Boros Legion.
Recruit: Bastion Defenders. When you issue the Recruit
order to this facility, you can recruit up to four new Bastion Defenders to fill the ranks of your Garrison. This recruitment incurs no monetary cost, ensuring that the Legion remains strong and vigilant.
Holy Forge of Razia
Level 5 Boros Legion Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 1
Order: Craft

The Holy Forge of Razia is a sacred space where weapons and armor are imbued with divine energy. Forged by master craftsmen, the equipment created here serves the Boros Legion’s mission of justice and righteousness.
Craft: Divine Armaments. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you can create one magical
weapon or armor piece of your choice, using the divine essence of Razia to enhance its properties. The crafting process takes 7 days and requires 100 GP for materials.
Judgement Hall
Level 5 Boros Legion Facility

Prerequisite: Rank 1 Renown with Boros Legion
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 1
Order: Empower

The Judgement Hall is a solemn chamber where decisions of law and justice are deliberated. Here,
characters can convene with Boros officials to interrogate captured foes or resolve disputes.
Empower: Righteous Decision. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, once per Bastion turn, the owning player character can hold a “Trial of Light” here. They gain Advantage on all Charisma based skill checks to persuade, intimidate, or compel truth from prisoners or individuals attending the trial. Successfully conducting a trial also increases morale among Bastion followers, granting Advantage on loyalty or morale checks with all NPCs in the Bastion for the next month.
Library of Aurelia’s Wisdom
Level 5 Bastion Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Research

The Library of Aurelia’s Wisdom is a vast repository of knowledge containing texts on tactics, law, and the history of the Boros Legion. Scholars and strategists delve into its depths to uncover insights that guide the Legion’s actions.
Research: Tactical Insights. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you may consult the library to gain Advantage on your next tactical decision in a Bastion Event or encounter.
Urban Underground Shadow Faith Performers
This is not a faction per se like the rest of them. These are options for multiple faction in Stickyickistan, and possibly available to individual characters regardless of faction membership. Generally up to our discretion, and it making sense narratively.
Lampooners Mirror Hall
Level 5 Cult of Rakdos Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Recruit

Stocked with conveniently placed mirrors so that the Lampooners of the Rakdos Cult can practice their jokes, satire, mockery, and puppet shows at any time. Many members of the Cult avoid this tent, lest they find scathing insults tested against them.
Recruit: Scathing Wit. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you may recruit up to two new Bastion Defenders from the Rakdos Lampooners (Guildmasters’ Guide to Ravnica, pg. 248).
Pleasure Quarters
Level 5 Cult of Rakdos Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Vast
Hirelings: 4
Order: Trade

The most above board money making scheme in the Cults book. The brothel tents are where
wealthy nobles are drawn, and fleeced for a night of distraction with their darkest fantasies. Often the Cult jokes that the rich are more demented than they are as a result from the many stories that have circulated.
Trade: Pleasures of the Flesh. When you issue the Trade order to this facility, roll 1d100 + 10, you earn this number in GP.
Performance Catalogs
Level 5 Cult of Rakdos Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 1
Order: Research

Filled with play scripts, this room is frequented by members of the Rakdos Cult that find themselves in need of inspiration or in need of an act quickly. This repository of all things Rakdos is one of few places where bloodshed and carnage don’t overrule sanity.
Research: Vile Inspiration. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you are granted
a +5 bonus to your next D20 Test that uses the Performance skill.
Roaring Acoustics
Level 5 Cult of Rakdos Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use an Arcane Focus or a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Vast
Hirelings: 4
Order: Harvest

Storing various materials and instructions, this room is key for enhancing the acoustics in the Bastion to ensure that every performance is as grand as possible, for Rakdos shall accept nothing less.
Empower: Light up the Stage. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, an enchanted aura washes over the Bastion, affecting all within it. You and anyone in the Bastion gain Advantage on D20 Tests requiring Charisma (Performance) for the next 7 days.
Stagehand Tent
Level 5 Cult of Rakdos Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Recruit

This roomy tent is packed with smaller rooms, each likely filled with weapons, instruments and other circus equipment. Here, new hands to the Rakdos cult practice their individual acts, honing their skills for the time when they get to act on stage.
Recruit: Stagehands. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you may recruit up to four
new Defenders, finding new Rakdos Performers (Guildmasters’ Guide to Ravnica, pg. 249).
Sideshow Stage
Level 5 Cult of Rakdos Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use a Holy Symbol or Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Vast
Hirelings: 3
Order: Harvest

Not the grand stage many expect when they think of a Rakdos performance, these smaller stages are used by up and coming performers who are honing their skills. A smaller spectacle, these acts are free to view but many leave tips following the show’s conclusion.
Harvest: Taste of Mayhem. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, you receive donations
in the form of gold and non-magical items. Select any combination of either gold and items from the Adventuring Gear table with a maximum combined value of 25 GP.
Tools of the Trade
Level 5 Cult of Rakdos Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Craft

Cluttered together are various workbenches used to design new costumes, build new tools for various acts and other tools for circus work are all made here.
Craft: Performance Gear. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you can craft 2 instruments or costumes. This process takes 7 days and incurs no monetary cost.
Zooka Mire Collective
Body Horror Warning. Any references to the Golgari swarm or locations can be flavored as a swamp or some myconid creature.
Bone Grafter
Level 5 Bastion Facility

Prerequisite: Corpses
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Craft

The Bone Grafter is as macabre as it sounds, a torchlit room with warm stone floors freshly spattered with blood and viscera leftovers used to feed the freshly made swarm creatures. Bone Grafters rend and tear bone from flesh to attach to the sentient fungal creatures and undead swarms that live in the Golgari caverns. Your Bone Grafting hirelings will outfit your Bastion Defenders with like-new armor from those who no longer need it.
Craft: Patchwork. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, your Bastion Defenders gain a +2 to their base AC. This costs one corpse per defender or 50 GP per defender. This effect does not stack over multiple uses.
Corpse Run Off
Level 5 Golgari Swarm Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Recruit

The Corpse Run Off is a grim, dimly lit space where the dead are collected from various disposal points and processed for use by the Golgari Swarm. Decaying bodies are dissected and their remains repurposed for the creation of undead soldiers or used in various dark rituals. The air is thick with the stench of rot, and only those who have truly embraced the Golgari philosophy of life, death, and rebirth find solace in its walls. Recruits who come here are steeped in the
practices of decay and rebirth, their loyalty to the Swarm solidified through their exposure to its most macabre aspects.
Recruit: Rebirth in Death. When you issue the Recruit order at this facility, you may raise 2d4 Zombies (D&D 2024 Free Rules pg. 359) under your control for 1 day, after which they decay into nothingness, or 2 Reclaimers (Guildmasters Guide to Ravnica pg. 234).
Fungal Chamber
Level 5 Golgari Swarm Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use an Arcane Focus or a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Empower

The Fungal Chamber is a damp, spore-infested room where fungal growths are cultivated and harnessed for magical purposes. The air is thick with spores that enhance the user’s connection to the arcane and divine, providing a unique source of power. Those who empower their magic in this chamber experience a symbiotic bond with the fungi, allowing them to channel the energies of decay and rebirth. The chamber is filled with the hum of living spores, and the walls are covered in bioluminescent fungi that glow softly in the dark.
Empower: Fungal Amplification. When you issue the Empower order at this facility, your spellcasting is enhanced by the magical properties of the fungi. Once per Long Rest, you may cast Entangle or Blight without expending a spell slot until your next Bastion turn.
Grotto Mortuary Market
Level 5 Golgari Swarm Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 3
Order: Trade

The Grotto Mortuary Market, an uncommon idea amongst those that desire death’s finality. However, this market trades in death and coin. ‘You need a body removed? Contact the Golgari, no one will ever find it…unless it walks up from the sewers.’ Many factions use the contacts within the Swarm to make problems disappear, it is often well compensated and the Swarm never asks many questions. Death is Death’s business, they are just the middleman.
Trade: Stiff Deals. When you issue the Trade order to this facility, you may either roll 1d100 and take the result as a percentage of profits, or roll 2d20 and take the result in corpses, or roll 1d4 and take the result in living prisoners.
Hive Nestuary
Level 5 Golgari Swarm Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Research

The Hive Nestuary, glows with an eerie sickly orange light from sinewy pustulant Oozes that take home here. They are tended to like one tends to a garden, however, these oozes are fed flesh and sometimes living prisoners. ‘Lips and tongues may lie but the flesh always tells the truth.’ You may commune with these nesting oozes to learn many insights.
Research: Saturated Thoughts. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you may find
useful information that provides you Advantage on D20 tests requiring Perception, Survival, and
History, for the next 48 hours. This action incurs no monetary cost.
Spore Garden
Level 5 Golgari Swarm Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use a Holy Symbol or Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Harvest

The Spore Garden is a dark and eerily tranquil space filled with vibrant, bioluminescent mushrooms and fungal life. Here, Spore Druids and Death Clerics channel their magic through the living fungus, drawing on the power of decay and rebirth. The spores imbue the spellcaster with enhanced magical energy, allowing them to grow stronger in their connection to the natural world.
Harvest: Fungal Harvest. When you issue the Harvest order at this facility, you may collect rare and
magical fungi that can be used as spell components or alchemical ingredients. Once per Long Rest, you may consume one of these rare fungi that grants a temporary benefit such as Advantage on a D20 Test or a bonus to your next spellcasting check at your DMs discretion.
Clans of the Outback
Arena of the Bloodpath
Level 5 Gruul Clans Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Vast
Hirelings: 4
Order: Recruit

The Arena of the Bloodpath is a vast open space where warriors of the Gruul Clans gather to test their strength and skill in battle. A Large, blood-soaked arena is surrounded by roaring crowds of gladiators, and the walls echo with the sounds of clashes between combatants. It is here that the Gruul recruit their fiercest warriors, seeking out those with raw power and a desire for destruction. Those who survive the trials are honored and empowered by the Clan.
Recruit: Bloodied Honor. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you may roll a d20 to determine the strength of a potential recruit. The stronger the roll, the more formidable the warrior, with a chance of gaining an additional benefit such as enhanced combat abilities or an increased loyalty score.
Grimshroud Trading Post
Level 5 Gruul Clans Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Vast
Hirelings: 3
Order: Trade

The Grimshroud Trading Post is a bustling marketplace, though far from the polished, refined exchanges of more civilized lands. Here, goods are traded with an air of danger and volatility, as Gruul traders barter with everything from scavenged weapons to rare herbs and potent magical artifacts. Though lawlessness prevails, there is a sense of mutual respect among the traders, and deals are struck under the looming threat of violence. The marketplace is located on the outskirts of Gruul territory, often near battlegrounds or sites of destruction, where the wreckage of war
fuels the trade.
Trade: Savage Deals. When you issue the Trade order to this facility, you may exchange resources,
equipment, or magical items. The items obtained here often come at a high cost, either in terms of danger or risk, but they hold unique, high-value properties. Once per Long Rest, you may acquire rare or unusual items, such as weapons or supplies scavenged from the battlefield, or magical objects imbued with primal energies determined by the DM.
Halls of Wild Lore
Level 5 Gruul Clans Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Research

The Halls of Wild Lore is a place of study and knowledge that is far from traditional libraries. The
Halls are carved into the heart of ancient trees and surrounded by thickets of vines, and inside, Gruul scholars study the nature of wild magic, beasts, and the elemental forces that shape the world. Rather than dusty books and scrolls, the Halls are filled with living records—ancient druidic symbols, runic inscriptions, and strange, sentient creatures that have been captured and brought to the Clans for study. The focus here is on the untamed forces that drive the Gruul Clans’ destructive power.
Research: Primal Secrets. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you uncover knowledge on primal magic, beast control, or the elements. This can provide insights into the mysteries of nature, rituals to enhance your abilities, or new methods to harness the forces of destruction. Once per Long Rest until your next Bastion turn, you gain the ability to Wild Shape into a Batterboar (Basic Rule 2014, pg. 131).
Pit of the Wastes
Level 5 Gruul Clans Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Harvest

The Pit of the Wastes is a toxic and desolate environment, full of scavengers, wild beasts, and
the refuse of nature. Here, the Gruul harvest rare resources, scavenging materials and creatures that have been discarded by the land. This pit is a source of power, where the primal nature of the Gruul Clans is tapped to make use of everything, no matter how corrupted or wasted.
Harvest: Wasteland Bounty. When you issue the Harvest order at this facility, you may gather unique, resourceful materials from the environment, such as rare herbs or mutated creatures. During your Bastion turn, you may gain 1d8 rare alchemical or crafting materials from this facility.
Rite of Raging Fire
Level 5 Gruul Clans Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Empower

The Rite of Raging Fire is a ritualistic chamber where fire magic is used to ignite the spirits of the
Gruul Clans. This blazing, fiery room is charged with destructive energy, allowing those who enter to tap into the primal rage of the fire elemental. Fire mages and warriors alike undergo rituals here to strengthen their magical and physical prowess.
Empower: Fire’s Wrath. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you may invoke the
fiery power of the ritual. Until your next Bastion turn, Once per Long Rest, you may add Fire damage to one of your attacks or spells, increasing its damage by 2d6 Fire damage.
Skarrg Shredder
Level 5 Gruul Clans Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use an Arcane Focus or a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 1
Order: Craft

The Skarrg Shredder is a chaotic forge, where the Gruul Clans craft weapons designed for both magical and physical destruction. This forge is dedicated to the creation of armaments infused with elemental fury, and it’s where powerful runes and elemental magic are inscribed onto weapons. Creators and spellcasters alike combine their expertise here to produce tools of devastation.
Craft: Shredder’s Edge. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you may create a weapon that carries the fury of the Gruul Clans. The weapon deals an additional 1d6 Elemental damage (chosen by you) for 24 hours, after which it reverts to its normal form.
Ashen Shadow Society
Cloak and Dagger
Level 5 House Dimir Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 1
Order: Recruit

The Cloak and Dagger room serves as a recruitment and training space for new Dimir hopefuls. Here, aspiring members hone their skills in stealth, infiltration, and subtlety.
Recruit: Hidden Operatives. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you can recruit up to four Dimir Spies (see Guildmaster’s Guide to Ravnica, pg. 232) as Bastion Defenders. These recruits operate in secrecy and are ready to deploy for covert missions at no monetary cost.
Ethereum Gardens
Level 5 House Dimir Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Harvest

The Ethereum Gardens cultivate rare, magical plants that assist with subtle manipulations of the mind and spirit. Agents harvest components here for use in spellcraft and alchemy.
Harvest: Veiled Elixirs. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, you gather ten vials of sleep inducing herbs or potions of minor illusions that aid in concealing objects or creatures (worth 5 GP each). Harvesting takes 7 days and incurs no monetary cost.
Obscured Laboratory
Level 5 House Dimir Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 1
Order: Craft

The Obscured Laboratory allows Dimir agents to create specialized toxins and alchemical concoctions used for espionage. Shadowy alchemists use it to prepare agents for missions that require subtlety and lethality.
Craft: Assassin’s Elixirs. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you can create 1d4 vials of Basic Poison or 1d4 doses of an elixir that grants temporary Advantage on D20 Tests requiring Dexterity (Stealth) for 24 hours. Crafting takes 7 days and incurs no monetary cost.
Enlarging the Facility: You can enlarge this facility to Roomy by spending 1000 GP. If you do so you
can increase the potency of the Poisons and Elixirs crafted in this space at the discretion of your DM.
Safehouse
Level 5 House Dimir Facility

Prerequisite: 1,000 GP
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Trade

The Safehouse is a discreetly hidden facility in a nondescript part of the city, camouflaged to blend
seamlessly with its surroundings. Accessible only by those with the proper codes and credentials,
this Safehouse serves as a critical node for Dimir operatives to trade valuable information, smuggle
goods, or lay low when needed. It’s a favored meeting point for guild members to conduct secret exchanges, stockpile equipment, and prepare for covert missions.
Trade: Hidden Channels. When you issue the Trade order to this facility, roll 1d100 to determine the outcome of a covert operation arranged through Dimir’s secret network. On a roll of 60 or higher, the operation yields either critical intelligence on a rival guild’s upcoming plans, a rare magical item, or high quality supplies worth up to 500 GP (DM’s choice). This facility provides a steady flow of resources for Dimir missions, all while keeping these exchanges invisible to prying eyes. This facility can also be used as a safe place for the player and adventuring party to rest within if they are within a 1 mile vicinity.
Shadowed Archive
Level 5 House Dimir Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to cast Divination spells
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Research

The Shadowed Archive is a covert library hidden within the Bastion, containing sensitive information, cryptic texts, and surveillance logs. Only trusted agents have access, using these resources to further Dimir’s objectives across Ravnica.
Research: Silent Surveillance. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you can consult
intelligence archives to gain Advantage on your next D20 Tests that use Wisdom (Insight) or Intelligence (Investigation) in a Dimir-related mission.
Shadowforge
Level 5 House Dimir Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Craft

The Shadowforge is a hidden and specialized forge designed for the creation of subtle, deadly weaponry and arcane tools that aid in infiltration. Darkly enchanted and soundproofed, this facility is equipped with shadow-infused metalwork and runes that hide the creations crafted here from magical detection.
Craft: Veiled Armaments. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you can create one magical
weapon or piece of gear with a Dimir-themed enchantment. Examples include the Dagger of Silence (grants Advantage on D20 Tests for Stealth and Silences targets on a critical hit for one round) or the Cloak of Shadows (grants +1 to Stealth and Advantage on D20 Tests against Detection Spells). This crafting process takes 7 days and requires 100 GP for materials.
Enlarging the Facility: You can enlarge this facility to Vast by spending 2000 GP. If you do so you can increase the rarity of the magic items crafted in this space at the discretion of your Dungeon Master.
Veil of Whispers
Level 5 House Dimir Facility

Prerequisite: Rank 1 Renown with House Dimir
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Empower

The Veil of Whispers is an enchanted chamber where secret communications and coded messages are crafted, sent, and received. It is used to transmit secure orders across Ravnica.
Empower: Silent Commands. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you gain the Message cantrip in the next Dimir Bastion Event or encounter where subterfuge is critical.
Enlarging the Facility: You can enlarge this facility to Vast by spending 2000 GP. If you do so you can increase the effects of Silent Commands to grant you and your Bastion Defenders the ability to use the Sending spell once per day during this Bastion turn and until the start of your next Bastion turn.
The Seekers of the Vein
Alchemical Anarchy Chamber
Level 5 Izzet League Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use a Holy Symbol or Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Harvest

The air of this room is choked in chemicals and alchemical fumes and when it’s not, it’s because
the smoke from a researcher’s latest explosive experiment has filled the room. In here the alchemists crowd the room with their instruments, working to make their next masterpiece.
Harvest: Mad Science. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, alchemists make either 10 vials of Alchemist Fire or 3 Potions of Healing.
Blastseeker Training Range
Level 5 Izzet League Facility

Prerequisite: Rank 2 renown with Izzet League
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Recruit

Endlessly in need of repairs, this yard is where the Blastseekers are outfitted, practice, and experiment with their armaments. The consistent explosions that tear the range apart serve well to remind others exactly how much firepower is in the Izzet armory, and how happy they would be to use it in combat.
Recruit: Blastseeker Arming. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you may recruit up to
four new Defenders, in any combination of Flux Blastseekers (Guildmasters’ Guide to Ravnica, pg. 242) and Galvanic Blastseekers (Guildmasters’ Guide to Ravnica, pg. 243). This recruitment incurs no
monetary cost.
Experiment Records
Level 5 Izzet League Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use an Arcane Focus or a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 2
Order: Research

A cramped archive of colorful records for various experiments over the Izzet League history rests here.
Research: Enlightening Notes. When you issue the Research order to this facility, for the next 24 hours you have Advantage on the first Constitution Saving Throw you make to maintain Concentration.
Guard Tower
Level 5 Izzet League Facility

Prerequisite: Rank 1 Renown with Izzet League
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Recruit

Overseeing the Bastion, the Guard Tower is where Defenders are stationed to ensure that no one
untoward to the Izzet League gets access to the laboratories.
Recruit: Watchtower Recruits. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you can recruit up to
four new Bastion Defenders to fill the ranks of your Garrison. This recruitment incurs no monetary cost, ensuring that the Legion remains strong and vigilant.
Nivmagus Laboratory
Level 5 Izzet League Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Vast
Hirelings: 2
Order: Craft

The main attraction of many Izzet Bastions, the labs. Characterized by dozens of mages going about to experimenting with their new theories and crafting new magical objects
Craft: Fruits of Labor. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you may make any one Uncommon magical item of your choice. This process takes 7 days and costs 200 GP. Typically these laboratories make Pyroconvergers (Guildmasters’ Guide to Ravnica, pg. 180) or a Mizzium
Apparatus (Guildmasters’ Guide to Ravnica, pg. 179).
Public Service Hall
Level 5 Izzet League Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Vast
Hirelings: 2
Order: Trade

Though the Izzet are well-known for their experimentation, they also have a hand in public
service. Here, the Izzet discuss commissions for building and modifying roadways, sewers, boilers,
and other infrastructure
Trade: Public Service. When you issue the Trade order to this facility, roll 1d100 - 10 and gain that number of GP to determine the profits the League made.
Testing Yard
Level 5 Izzet League Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Research

A heavily fortified yard where the Izzet researchers test new experiments. The hirelings here are specially trained to handle dangerous unknown equipment, which is to say they are heavily protected for explosions.
Research Options. When you issue the Research order to this facility you may select on of the
following choices:
Research: Weapon Experiments. Select one weapon, until you use this facility again you are proficient with that weapon.
Research: Armor Testing. Select one armor type, until you use this facility again you are proficient with that armor.
The Boilerpit
Level 5 Izzet League Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Cramped
Hirelings: 4
Order: Empower

Built into the basement of the Bastion, the League maintains a large boiler that provides hot water and heat to the rest of the Bastion. The boilers ensure that the Izzet League can enjoy certain comforts in their Bastion.
Empower: Boiler Overdrive. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you increase the
productivity of the boilers and as a side benefit, the Bastion becomes much warmer, further revitalizing members. This makes your Long Rests more effective, increasing the number of Hit Point Dice regained by 2.
Shadow Faiths General
Cathedral of Debt
Level 5 Orzhov Syndicate Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Empower

A dimly lit room with stained glass windows depicting bound spirits and haunted figures. The
Chamber of Binding Oaths is where sacred pacts are sealed in blood, binding both parties to their word under the gaze of the Orzhov’s spirits.
Empower: Pact of Obedience. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, you can perform a
ritual to seal a binding pact with a willing creature. For 7 days, this creature cannot break promises
made to you within the chamber without suffering a potent curse. The curse inflicts Disadvantage on all the creature’s rolls until they make amends or are absolved of their debt.
Crypt of Eternal Servitude
Level 5 Orzhov Syndicate Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Harvest

The Crypt is a somber chamber filled with the remains of those who could not repay their debts
in life and are now bound to serve in death. Ghostly apparitions linger, awaiting commands.
Harvest: Ghostly Servitude. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, spectral spirits rise from the crypt to serve your Bastion. For the next 7 days, these spirits perform mundane tasks within the Bastion, granting your Bastion Advantage on D20 Tests made to prevent negative Bastion events.
Hall of Whispered Secrets
Level 5 Orzhov Syndicate Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Research

The Hall of Whispered Secrets is a shadowy library containing scrolls of forbidden knowledge and
hidden truths. Its shelves are filled with confidential information and blackmail material.
Research: Secrets of Influence. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you can spend 7
days gathering arcane and political knowledge. You gain Advantage on D20 Tests requiring Insight and Investigation related to uncovering secrets, and you gain temporary proficiency in one Intelligence-based skill of your choice for the next 7 days.
Shrine of the Debt Collector’s Grace
Level 5 Orzhov Syndicate Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Harvest

A modest shrine adorned with icons of spectral figures and adorned with offerings from those
seeking forgiveness. The Shrine of the Debt-Collector’s Grace is where the desperate pray for
absolution of their debts.
Harvest: Offerings of Absolution. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, petitioners seeking to reduce spiritual debts provide offerings. At the end of 7 days, you collect 1d6 × 10 GP in donations. Additionally, the shrine provides one free casting of the Lesser Restoration spell during the week.
Enlarging the Facility: You can enlarge this facility to Vast by spending 2000 GP. If you do so, gain 1d6 x 100 GP in donations.
Vault of Greed
Level 5 Orzhov Syndicate Facility

Prerequisite: 2000 GP or at least 2 uncommon magic items
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Trade

The Vault of Greed is a heavily guarded chamber housing treasures, relics, and artifacts accumulated by the Orzhov over generations.
Trade: Display of Wealth. When you issue the Trade order to this facility , you open the Vault to visitors who pay for access. At the end of the week, roll 1d100 to determine your earnings (1d100 x 10 GP). The vault’s prestige grants you Advantage on Charisma based D20 Tests for the next 7 days.
Enlarging the Facility: You can enlarge this facility to Vast by spending 2000 GP or donating 2 uncommon magic items. If you do so you can choose to make the effect of Display of Wealth change to the following. At the end of the week, roll 1d100 to determine your spendings (1d100 x 10 GP). You gain an uncommon magic randomly rolled on the Magic Item table by the DM per 100 GP spent.
The Old Faiths
Archives of Mat’Selesnya
Level 5 Selesnya Conclave Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Research

The Archives of Mat’Selesnya house a wealth of knowledge and lore passed down through the
generations. This facility contains teachings on nature magic, druidic practices, and Selesnya
philosophy, helping guild members learn from their predecessors.
Research: Spiritual Insight. When you issue the Research order to this facility, you consult the
archives to gain Advantage on your next Wisdom based D20 Test during a Bastion Event or encounter.
Conclave Greenhouses
Level 5 Selesnya Conclave Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Craft

The Conclave Greenhouses are a carefully tended sanctuary where rare plants and herbs are grown with the aid of Selesnya Druids. This facility is essential for cultivating natural ingredients used in creating potent healing and alchemical mixtures.
Craft: Soothing Potions. When you issue the Craft order to this facility, you can create 2d4 Potions of Healing or 1 Potion of Growth (or a similar plant-based potion, per the DM’s discretion). Crafting takes 7 days and incurs no monetary cost.
Garden of Vitality
Level 5 Selesnya Conclave Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use a Druidic Focus
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Empower

The Garden of Vitality is a peaceful oasis where plants, animals, and Selesnya members gather to
share in nature’s bounty. Filled with vibrant flowers and lush greenery, this facility rejuvenates and
revitalizes those who walk its paths.
Empower: Natural Renewal. When you issue the Empower order to this facility, all allies who rest
in this garden gain the benefits of the Lesser Restoration spell, and additionally gain temporary
hit points equal to your level plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). This effect lasts for the
next 24 hours.
Enlarging the Facility: You can enlarge this facility to Vast by spending 5000 GP. If you do so you can increase the potency of the effects of Natural Renewal to the following: All allies who rest in this garden gain the benefits of the Greater Restoration spell, and temporarily increase their Maximum Hit Points equal to your level plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). This effect lasts until your next Bastion turn.
Glade of Kinship
Level 5 Selesnya Conclave Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Recruit

In the heart of your Bastion lies the Glade of Kinship, a tranquil, lush space imbued with the welcoming energy of the Conclave. Here, Druids, Priests, and new guild initiates gather for bonding rituals and community celebrations, reinforcing the spirit of unity and shared purpose. In this grove, potential recruits find a sense of belonging and devotion to the Conclave’s mission of harmony.
Recruit: Kin of the Conclave. When you issue the Recruit order to this facility, you may call upon 4 new initiates or caretakers to join your Bastion. These new members serve as messengers, scouts, or apprentice Druids, ready to support Bastion activities and defend the sanctuary if needed. These Defenders use the Horncaller (Guildmasters Guide to Ravnica pg.253) statblock, and their training takes 7 days, incurring no monetary cost.
Special Benefit: While the Glade of Kinship is active, each recruit gains a bonus +1 to Wisdom-based D20 Tests made within the Bastion, representing the Conclave’s influence on their Insight and Perception.
Sacred Grove
Level 5 Selesnya Conclave Facility

Prerequisite: None
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 1
Order: Harvest

The Sacred Grove is a secluded and tranquil area within the Bastion, where plants, animals, and fey
creatures are nurtured by druidic magic. The grove resonates with primal energy, cultivating plants with potent healing properties.
Harvest: Healing Herbs. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, you gather enough herbs to create 1d4 Potions of Healing or 1 Potion of Greater Healing. Harvesting takes 7 days and incurs no monetary cost.
Voda’s Healing Pool
Level 5 Selesnya Conclave Facility

Prerequisite: Ability to use a Holy Symbol or Druidic Focus
Space: Roomy
Hirelings: 2
Order: Harvest

Voda’s Healing pool is a tranquil retreat where wounded and weary adventurers can receive the
blessings of Selesnya’s healing magic. The Pool is a place of meditation, where sacred waters cleanse and rejuvenate those who bathe within.
Harvest: Blessed Waters. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, you can collect three vials of holy water or one vial of a specially blessed elixir that restores 1d4 hit points each hour for 4 hours. Harvesting takes 7 days and incurs no monetary cost.

Misc/Conditions-of-Drakkenheim.title: Conditions of Drakkenheim
Misc/Conditions-of-Drakkenheim.content:
Addled
You have Disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma attacks rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.
Bewildered
You can’t cast spells, except for cantrips with a casting time of 1 action.
Bleeding (X)
You’re losing blood to an open wound.

Ongoing Damage. At the end of each of your turns, you lose Hit Points. The number of Hit Points lost is indicated by the condition, such as “Bleeding 2d4.”
Regaining Hit Points. The condition ends if you regain any Hit Points.
Medical Treatment. You or another creature within 5 feet of you can spend an action and use a healer’s kit to staunch the bleeding (no check required), ending the condition.

Bloodied
You’re wounded. A creature is Bloodied while it has half its Hit Points or fewer remaining.
Burning (X)
You’re on fire or covered in acid:

Ongoing Damage. At the end of each of your turns, you take damage. The damage type and amount are indicated by the condition, such as “Burning (4d6 Fire)” or “Burning (2d4 Acid).”
Ending the Condition. The condition ends if you or another creature within 5 feet of you can spend an action to extinguish the flames or scrape off the acid, or if some other effect douses the flames (such as being submerged in water).

Clumsy
You have Disadvantage on Dexterity attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.
Contamination
While you have Contamination, you experience the following effects.
Contamination Levels. This condition is cumulative. Each time you receive it, you gain one or more levels of Contamination. You undergo a Monstrous Transformation if your Contamination level reaches 6.
Contamination Symptoms. A Contaminated creature suffers the symptoms from its current level as well as all lower levels. Conditions gained from Contamination end when those Contamination levels end. There is no other way to remove conditions caused by symptoms of Contamination.
Contamination Symptoms

































LevelSymptoms1None2Halve the Hit Points you regain when you expend Hit Dice during a Short Rest3You do not regain Hit Points when you finish a Long Rest.4You have the  condition.5You have the  condition.6Monstrous Transformation!
Mutations. Each time you gain a Contamination level, roll 1d6. If the result is equal to or lower than your current Contamination level, you gain a randomly determined mutation by rolling on the Mutations Table. The effects of the mutation remain while you have Contamination levels. Unless otherwise specified, a creature can’t gain the same mutation more than once. If a duplicate result is rolled, the GM chooses a different one or rolls again.
Dazed
You can move or take an action on your turn, not both. You can’t take Bonus Actions.
Defenseless
Attack rolls against you have Advantage.
Distracted
You can’t take Reactions.
Drakkenheim Madness
A character with Drakkenheim Madness gains one of the following traits:

Storm Troll

“I wish I didn’t have all these useless organs inside me.”
“The contamination is a blessing which will transform me into a wondrous creature.”
“The monsters are civilians trying to live a peaceful life! We need to protect them!”
“I must wear a flesh-coat made from my slain enemies to gain their strength!”
“My companions died in the ruins. I’m sorry friends, you are merely ghosts haunting me, you aren’t real. Stop trying to talk to other people.”
“I need to eat everything I can find. It’s probably going to be my last meal.”
“Drakkenheim is so beautiful at night. I could spend forever wandering the streets by moonlight. We should go tonight! Let’s go every night!”
“Don’t you fools get it?! If you die in Drakkenheim, you die IN REAL LIFE!!!!”
“A sinister cabal of disembodied hands is plotting against me.”
“I must go into the ruins and kill. Rip and tear, until it is done.”

Enfeebled
You have Disadvantage on Strength attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.
Frozen (DC X)
You’re partially encased in ice:

You’re Immobilized and Defenseless.
You’re Helpless against attacks made with a weapon that deals Bludgeoning damage.
You or another creature take an action to break the ice away. To do so, you must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) check. On a successful check, the condition ends. The DC is indicated by the condition, such as Frozen (DC 15).
This condition ends on you if you take 20 Bludgeoning or Fire damage.

Helpless

Any attack that hits you is a Critical Hit.

Immobilized

Your Speed becomes 0, and you can’t benefit from any bonuses to your Speed.
If you’re flying when you become Immobilized, you fall.

Jinxed (X)
Roll the die indicated by the condition, such as “Jinxed 1d4” each time you make an attack roll or saving throw. Subtract the value on the die from the result.
Shocked

You’re Dazed and Defenseless.
You drop whatever you’re holding in your hands.
You must spend an action to draw, stow, or pick up an object.

Sickened
You have Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws.
Slowed
Your Speed is halved.
Staggered
You can’t make more than one weapon attack during your turn, regardless of your class features, spells, or magic items.
Valor (X)
Add a die to your attack rolls and saving throws. The die rolled is specified by the condition, such as Valor (1d4).
Weakened
You deal half damage with weapon attacks and spells.

Misc/Delerium.title: Delerium
Misc/Delerium.content:
Delerium is a magical mineral left behind by the meteor that landed in Drakkenheim. It is the antithesis of Arcanite. It appears in geode clusters of translucent, sharp-edged crystals which reflect octarine light. The eldritch stones softly hum in dissonant tones, and glow brightly at night or when exposed to magic. Deposits are found throughout Drakkenheim, often fused into stone streets and buildings like crystalline moss.
A typical delerium fragment is about the size of a finger. Crystals may be fist-sized or slightly larger, and geodes may be as big as a pumpkin. Massive clusters might grow taller than a human.
Delerium Crystals




































































Crystal SizeMarket Value (Buy)WeightACHPExtraction TimeStabilization DCChip30 gold1/4 lbs1551 action8Fragment80 gold1/2 lbs17101 minute12Shard300 gold1 lbs19155 minutes16Crystal1,600 gold2 lbs212030 minutes20Geode8,000 gold20 lbs +23251 hour24Massive ClusterPriceless8,000 lbs +25507 days28
Delerium Properties
All delerium samples have the following traits regardless of size:

Immune to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage; as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from non-magical weapons.
Resistant to Acid, Cold, Fire, and Lightning damage; as well as Slashing and Piercing damage from magical weapons.
Vulnerable to Bludgeoning damage from magical weapons.
Unless contained within an Antimagic Field, delerium shatters and crumbles into worthless ash when reduced to 0 Hit Points. However, delerium geodes release a random Arcane Anomaly when destroyed (see below).

Delerium Hazards
When a humanoid creature touches delerium without protective gear for the first time on their turn, or ends their turn in bodily contact with delerium, they must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 Necrotic damage and gain one level of Contamination, as described earlier in this appendix.
Delerium Harvesting
Delerium found in Drakkenheim is usually fused into the ground or stone buildings. It is carefully extracted using handheld mining equipment such as shovels, picks, hammers, and chisels. Consult the table to determine how long it takes characters to extract delerium. Lacking proper equipment, extraction takes ten times as long. Massive clusters are impossible to extract without heavy equipment or powerful magic.
Uses for Delerium
Delerium has vast arcane potential. Beyond trade, crystals are used for several purposes:
Spell Component. Delerium may be used as an arcane focus or material component for any spell on the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. When casting a spell which requires a costly material component, a spellcaster may instead use delerium of equivalent or greater value to the required cost.
Magic Items. Delerium is an exceptional material for creating magical items of all kinds. Any existing magic item described in the Basic Rules could be made with delerium. Fragments, shards, crystals, and geodes may be used to make uncommon, rare, very rare, and legendary items respectively.
Stable Delerium. The process for crafting magic items with delerium renders the crystals stable, effectively turning it into Arcanite. Unless otherwise specified, characters do not take damage nor risk Contamination when they touch or handle stable delerium. Stable delerium is damaged and destroyed in the same manner as a normal magic item of its kind. Enough Stability Serum costs 50% of the buying price of the shard. If an attempt at stabilizing a shard is made outside an Antimagic Field and fails, the shard turns to dust. If the attempt fails by 5 or more, the shard explodes dealing VDAM necrotic damage and applying 1 level of contamination to any creature within 10 feet.
Delerium Dust. Delerium dust is usually made by grinding the crystals against one another to create a fine powder. This milling process is extraordinarily hazardous unless performed within an Antimagic Field. Delerium dust can be used in alchemy, as a spell component, a reagent for brewing potions, or mixed into inks used to scribe spell scrolls.
Improvised Weapons & Ammunition. Delerium fragments may be used as ammunition for a sling or fashioned into a makeshift club. Such weapons and ammunition deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage, and humanoid creatures struck must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of Contamination. Delerium used as ammunition in this way is destroyed.
Delicate Balance of the Elements
Arcanite and Delerium are like yin and yang. Arcanite represents order, and light while Delerium represents darkness, and chaos. Arcanite’s magical properties are perfectly stable making it very reliable at powering most magitech, but slightly less powerful and much more expensive. Delerium on the other hand is a highly volatile element allowing it to output more magical energy for powering magitech, but not as reliable and much more dangerous.

Misc/Edicts-of-Lumen.title: Edicts of Lumen
Misc/Edicts-of-Lumen.content:
During antiquity, mighty sorcerer-kings ruled a continent-spanning empire using their immense arcane power. However, this empire was entirely unaware of the isolated lands of Stickyickistan, and the Islands of Y’ummm. The sorcerer-kings became tyrants who scarred the land with magical wars and held those without arcane magical power in bondage. The iron rule of the sorcerer-kings was ended by the clerics and paladins of The Faith of the Sacred Flame a thousand years ago. However, those born with arcane magical ability have faced discrimination ever since, and at times, the religious ministry has endorsed vicious persecution against mages. Even today, many common folk consider a Mageborn child a terrible curse. It was these ideals that drove Human Colonialism into Stickyickistan, but when Stickyickistan gained independence from Elyria, the Edicts ceased to be enforced. Those who follow the faith have labelled Stickyickistanians as heretical hedonists, or gold worshippers.
Outright conflict ended with the Edicts of Lumen, a magical treaty between the Amethyst Academy, the continental nobility, and the Faith of the Sacred Flame. Signed three centuries ago, this agreement separates the political and economic powers of clergy, mages, and nobles.
The Edicts of Lumen comprise six main articles:

The Articles of Inheritance bar all mages from holding noble titles or owning land.
The Articles of Neutrality require the Amethyst Academy remain neutral and impartial with regards to the social, economic, and political affairs of the continent, but also grant protection under the law to all mages.
The Articles of Guardianship grant the Amethyst Academy the authority to take any child born with magical capabilities as wards to train in magic until they come of age, including Mageborn of noble houses and royalty.
The Articles of Enterprise permit the Amethyst Academy to operate as a self-governing mage guild to control the sale of magical goods and arcane magical services throughout the continent, but they may not discriminate or charge their clients differently.
The Articles of Malediction disallow the Academy from teaching magical practices such as summoning demons and creating undead, and forbid mages from using magic to directly influence or control members of the nobility or clergy.
The Articles of Umbrage detail a complex system for resolving minor infractions in a peaceful manner, reparations for damages for more serious violations, and the circumstances when parties may use violent force to enforce compliance.

Misc/Elder-Caps.title: Elder Caps
Misc/Elder-Caps.content: Elder Caps are magical mushrooms of a divine nature.

Misc/Fist.title: Fist
Misc/Fist.content:
Texas Hold ‘em Poker d6 adaptation.
Dictionary

Fist = Hand
SB = Small Blind
BB = Big Blind

Playing
A big and small blind will be identified by using d20 rolls. Highest in roll is small blind, and the next highest is big blind. Ante won’t scale throughout the game for simplicity sake. Minimum buy in is 50gp, maximum is 500gp. SB pays 1gp, and BB pays 2gp to start the pot, then everyone rolls 2d6 to themselves (and GM). Based on these rolls the players can take the normal poker actions of call, raise, fold. After all pre-flop actions are taken the house dealer rolls the 3d6 flop, and the game progresses as a normal poker game would with players connecting a 5d6 “Fist” with their 2d6 and 3d6 from the board. Fists are as follows from highest to lowest:
Fists Best to Worst

Five-of-a-kind
Four-of-a-kind
Full House
Straight
Three-of-a-kind
Two-pair
Pair

Misc/Heliana's-Guide-to-Monster-Hunting.title: Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting
Misc/Heliana's-Guide-to-Monster-Hunting.content:
Player Overview
Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting is a third-party D&D supplement from The Loot Tavern that the Free League of Stickyickistan uses heavily for monster hunts, crafting, harvesting, unusual magic items, subclasses, spells, and weird creature-driven adventures.
The book is built around the idea that monsters are not just obstacles. They are mysteries to investigate, dangerous encounters to survive, and valuable sources of materials if you know how to harvest them. A typical Heliana-style adventure might involve tracking a creature, learning its habits, preparing for its abilities, fighting it, then using parts of the monster to craft potions, gear, magic items, or other rewards.
For players, this means:

Monster hunts may involve investigation, preparation, and research before combat.
Creatures may have special traits, phases, weaknesses, or unusual rewards.
Harvesting monster parts can matter.
Crafting and alchemy may be more important than in a standard D&D game.
Some species options, spells, items, and subclasses may come from Loot Tavern material.
Always ask your DM before assuming a Heliana option is available for your character.

In the Free League, Heliana’s content is treated as part of the campaign’s extended toolbox. It fits Stickyickistan well because it supports strange monsters, magical biology, dangerous ingredients, and rewards that feel more interesting than just “you find gold.”
Links

Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting
[Loot Tavern Website]((loottavern.com/)
Loot Tavern Patreon

An Extraplanar Bestseller
In-universe, Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting also exists as a wildly popular adventuring manual, field guide, and coffee-table hazard across the planes. Copies have been found in Oeridian monster hunters’ lodges, Faerûnian wizard towers, Ansaloni taverns, noble Thranish libraries, Sigilite marketplaces, and the backpacks of people who absolutely should have read more than the first chapter before accepting a job.
The book is advertised as an “extraplanar bestseller,” though no one is entirely sure which planes are included in the sales numbers. Different editions are known to contain contradictory marginal notes, suspicious stains, regional monster warnings, and occasional advice that seems to update itself after a reader survives something awful.
Among adventurers, owning a copy is considered both practical and ominous. It usually means you are either preparing to hunt a monster, pretending to know how to hunt a monster, or about to become a cautionary sidebar in the next printing.
Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting
Wondrous Item, varies
Full of useful knowledge and heavy enough to crush a skull, Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting is nothing if not handy. The personalised quotes from Heliana, Peeper’s deft proofing and editing, and the numerous ink stains and spilled watercolours give this hefty tome a homemade feel.
Fantastic Phalanges and Where to Find Them. As an action, you can open this book and stare intently at its pages, which turn of their own accord to settle on an anatomical diagram of the corpse nearest to the book. You immediately learn all the harvestable parts of the corpse, as well as their Component DCs.
Know Thy Enemy. As an action, you can place an object that belonged to a creature—such as its scat, scales, or clothing— between the pages of this book. One minute later, the book tells you a piece of information about the creature (number determined by rarity). At the GM’s discretion, this may be: its saving throw proficiencies, damage resistances, immunities, and vulnerabilities; condition immunities; creature’s type; one of its traits; or one of the clues acquired during a hunt. Placing more objects that belonged to that creature (or a creature with the same statblock) yields no further results.
Weapon of the Learned. This book can be used as a simple melee weapon that deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage on a hit. If you are proficient in Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion, you are proficient with this weapon.
Anatomiser (Very-rare). If you read this book for 1 hour, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice for the next 24 hours: Arcana, Investigation, Nature, Medicine, Religion, or Survival. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again for 24 hours.
Applicable Items




















NameRarityPriceHeliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (Uncommon)Uncommon150 gp (~500 gp if purchased outside The Loot Tavern)Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting (Very Rare)Very Rare3,100 gp

Misc/Lean.title: Lean
Misc/Lean.content: Lean is a special Alcoholic concoction created by the Shadow Wizard Money Gang. Lean is a mixed drink consisting mostly of soda, but the money spell shadow alchemists in the gang have created an incredibly high proof, thick, sweet smelling, alcoholic syrup they pour into the soda. This mix has become a trend with some sub-cultures of youths in Stickyickistan since the gang affiliated music group BASED NEGATIVE SQUAD popularized its consumption along with their fashion sense.

Misc/Magebred-Animals.title: Magebred Animals
Misc/Magebred-Animals.content:
Description
Magebred animals are magically bred by House Northbourne to have useful qualities. Northbourne has bred them through generations of arcane experiments. Magebred animals resemble fine specimens of the base animals, and some possess unusual colorations that may not be found in nature and exaggerates the desired feature.
Abilities
Magebred animals are easier to handle than normal animals, and are excellent learners of tricks and take well to training. They are stronger, more dexterous, and more resilient than others. Breeds of magebred animals possess a few differing special qualities, which may include one of the below:

Swift: This breed of magebred animal are faster than normal.
Thick-Skinned Breed: This breed of magebred animal has tougher natural armor.
Tracking: This breed of magebred animal is more skilled at following tracks.

Ecology
The magebred animals are generally bred to create better animals that are more suited for daily life. Some experiments in magebreeding have led to new magical beasts with surprising intelligence, and supernatural or spell-like abilities. The vast majority of magebred animals in Stickyickistan originate in the stables of House Northbourne’s estate in North Booftown. Some magebred animals have escaped into the wild, where they become ill-tempered and territorial.

Misc/Magitech.title: Magitech
Misc/Magitech.content:
In Stickyickistan, Magitech is the lifeblood of progress, industry, and warfare—a volatile fusion of arcane energy and mechanical ingenuity that has propelled the city-state into a new era of power and excess. Fueled by Arcanite and Delerium, the rare magical ore harvested from Mount Zooka, Magitech ranges from simple enchanted tools to experimental war machines, reshaping daily life and the balance of power.
The city’s greatest minds—the Arkanitech Guild, rogue artificers, and criminal syndicates—compete to push Magitech further, creating clockwork constructs, arcane firearms, and reality-warping enchantments that blur the line between magic and machinery. The wealthy elite on Nevercough Island flaunt their personal teleportation sigils and self-mending garments, while the slums of Upper South Booftown repurpose discarded Magitech scraps into makeshift weapons and illicit contraptions.
But Magitech is as unstable as it is revolutionary. Faulty enchantments lead to catastrophic explosions, experimental constructs gain sentience and go rogue, and overloaded Arcanite batteries have turned entire neighborhoods into ashes. Despite the risks, Stickyickistan’s hunger for innovation and power ensures that Magitech will only continue to evolve—for better or worse.

Misc/Spiritwax.title: Spiritwax
Misc/Spiritwax.content:
Spiritwax is an Alcoholic alchemical creation of Xon that allows the illicit product to be packaged in easy to transport bricks of a wax-like substance. The recipe is mixed and brewed inside a mold, where it hardens into the shape of the mold which is usually either bricks or candles. The bricks of product can be melted back into a liquid form to be consumed through a process determined by the magical ingredients, and the brewer of the batch. some melt by flame, some require a solvent, some may require something else.
Recipe
Mundane Ingredients
All are required and cost a total of 5 gp.

beeswax
distilled alcohol
pine resin
a pinch of powdered amber

Magical Ingredients
Only one of these is required. they are DC 5 components, and have a base cost of 10 gp.

Phial of sap (plant)
Phial of congealed blood (undead)
Phial of acid (ooze, explosive)
Phial of blood (any)
Pouch of dust (fiend, celestial)
Primordial dust (elemental, potentially explosive)
Phial of oil (construct, explosive)

Mechanics


Each brick could hold one gallon of alcohol (25 gp market value).


Bricks weigh half as much as liquid casks and are far less conspicuous.


Mishandling (exposure to the wrong flame, too much flame, a volatile solvent, or breaking the brick) could cause spoiling or explosions depending on the magical ingredients.


The reversal process is determined by the tool the brewer/alchemist uses, and the assosciated skill check of the monster type the magical ingredient was harvested from. This process is esoteric, and must be shared with a buyer if they are to be able to liquify the brick. You may want to give a buyer the same recipe each time for consistency, or maybe you switch it up regularly so no one can catch on to a pattern.
ex. if Alchemist’s Tools are used, and the magical ingredient is a phial of congealed blood from an Undead, then a creature that has Alchemist Tools proficiency, and Medicine proficiency can add their proficiency bonus for both to the Intelligence check to complete the reversal process. A creature without those proficiencies would just make an Intelligence roll.

Misc/The-Silt-Road.title: The Silt Road
Misc/The-Silt-Road.content:
Is not literally a road the name is a metaphor for the trail of illicit trade from Stickyickistan to the Underdark below.
The name comes from the fact that most of the wealth made on the market comes from mining. Arcanite in particular, but other things as well.
Sometimes, unlicensed individuals, and small mining outfits will enter the licensed jurisdiction of larger mining companies like The Seekers of the Vein, and other subsidiaries of House Stonemug, to steal what they can find of value, and re-sell on the Silt Road.
Of course gems, and precious metals aren’t the only illicit product you can find on this infamous trade route
Alcohol being the most popular of any illegal substance in the realm can of course be found up and down the Silt Road. From the smallest trade outpost to Molten Maw, they all wish for a taste of the forbidden barley juice.

Misc/Zooka-Malt.title: Zooka Malt
Misc/Zooka-Malt.content:
Zooka Malt is a beverage similar to ale that is made by alchemically fermenting a biomantic plant called Humulus Lupulus with fruits and spices. The effects of drinking Zooka Malt are mechanically the same as drinking alcohol, but it is half as potent. For flavour, the effects of Zooka Malt are comparable to the effects of CBD, or Melatonin. A small hint of euphoria with an increasingly overwhelming urge to crawl into bed. Refer to Heliana’s Guide for drunkenness rules.
Humulus Lupulus. is a member of the Arcannabaceae family of flowering biomantic plants. It is often misidentified as it’s much more famous cousin, Arcannabis, because of the way it looks, but Humulus Lupulus does not have the same arcane properties. This plant is mainly used in brewery for its flavour, and mundane medicinal value of being antibacterial.

Mythmos.title: Mythmos
Mythmos.content:
Mythmos is an oblate sphere of rock and water with an Arcanite core that orbits a fiery sun called Lumytholaris (loo-mi-tho-law-ris). It has one moon, and a few other celestial neighbours in Lumytholarispace, but they are all largely uninhabited. Most trips outside the mythic atmosphere of Mythmos are mining expeditions for rare cosmic elements. Trace amounts of Arcanite and Delerium can be found in the solar system’s asteroid belt. Sages from across the realms have put forth differing theories to explain the order of the cosmos throughout history. These included bizarre concepts such as the “great wheel”, the “world axis”, the “conjunction of the spheres”, “planetary orbits”, and “general relativity”. There is no consensus; every theorist is quick to point out the glaring flaws and logical inconsistencies in competing hypotheses.
Realms of Mythmos
The people who inhabit the planet of Mythmos simply call it “the earth” or “the world”. They live on “the continent” that is divided into several nations which people refer to as “the realms”. The largest and most politically influential of these sovereign states are Caspia, Elyria, and Westemär. Neighbouring each are several petty kingdoms and dozens of city states such as Stickyickistan and Liberio.

Stickyickistan
Stickyickistan can be found on the map of the continent in the Middle Sea off the Gold Coast.
Westemär
The Realm of Westemär stretches north from the Drakeclaw and Glimmer Mountains, along the Crystal Coast to northern tundras. The heartland is made up of deep dark forests surrounding wide flowing rivers, interspersed with areas of fertile marshland. The land is prosperous and rich in natural resources: iron, salt, and coal mines, fine timber, and excellent quarries. These industries supported the realm’s once-great military strength and built the impressive architecture of its cities. As such, the nobility are distinguished, but materialistic and prideful, in contrast to the hard-working and pragmatic common folk.
A Broken Realm
Spliffholm was the capital of Westemär and home to the ruling family, House von Kessel. After the meteor fell, the two surviving scions of House von Kessel clashed over succession in a brutal civil war that tore the nation apart. After many assassinations, accidents, and disastrous battles, the civil war ended with no clear victor. Most believe House von Kessel is now extinct, and the throne remains abandoned and empty in the ruins of Castle Drakken.
