Festivals celebrating both the halflings’ reverence for nature and the humans’ entrepreneurial spirit became the heartbeat of the city-state, uniting the population under a shared sense of identity. This is not to say that all racial tensions have gone away.
Stickyickistan, with its majestic architecture, aromatic markets, and vibrant streets, stands today as a testament to the resilience and adaptability of its people. The island’s history, forever marked by the invasion and subsequent coexistence, serves as a reminder of the complexities of cultural exchange and the potential for harmony amidst disparate communities.
As the waves lap against the shores of Stickyickistan, the echoes of its past reverberate through the bustling city streets. The legacy of the halflings’ ancestral connection to the land and the humans’ quest for prosperity interweave to form the fabric of this remarkable island city-state, forever entwined with the enigmatic allure of Arcanite.
The Making of a City State
Stickyickistan wasn’t always a city state. it was once a nation with multiple population centers. The main Human settlement on Nevercough Island was named Nevercough City after their patriarchal noble family. A Dwarf settlement was excavated into the base of Mount Zooka across the Percolat Inlet from Nevercough City which they named Bongstad. Then there was the native Halflings reserved land which was not given an official name, but it was positioned right between a giant lava river, and the slopes of Mount Zooka making it barely habitable.
Those settlements were all more or less on the coast of the nation, but there was one more settlement being setup much further inland, Spliffholm. This city settlement was started by a legendary Twothirdlings bard Jimmyjock Labingi. At its height, Spliffholm rivaled Nevercough City itself, producing magically enhanced warships, towering arcane ballistae, and nature-infused war machines. Spliffholm grew into a bastion of hope for the indigenous population, and stood firmly in the way of complete Elyrian domination. Spliffholm eventually became a major economic competitor with Nevercough City since they valued both settler and indigenous knowledge. This lead to rising political tensions between the two burgeoning governments and there have been many conspiracy theories regarding the real motives behind the Blight. Some speculate that it was a covert operation conducted by the Tribunal Highblade Coalition to frame Valmorra the Hollowed for the act of terrorism among other theories.
The Arcane Civil War and the Cataclysm
As power struggles erupted on the island, the region fell into civil war. Industrial sabotage, magical duels, and full-scale battles tore the city apart, with factions summoning fiends, creating unstable war golems, and using necromantic plagues to gain the upper hand.
At the peak of the conflict, it is said that the Necromancer of Zuggtmoy, Valmorra the Hollowed, unleashed her ultimate weapon—the Emerald Blight, a magical plague that turned the living into mindless, fungal-infested undead. While her intent was to control the fallen, the Blight quickly spiraled out of control, transforming Spliffholm into a nightmarish wasteland of rotting, deathless horrors.
Realizing the catastrophe would consume all of Stickyickistan, an unlikely alliance of native Halfling druids, Ashenfey, Verdanfey, Elemental creatures, and arcanists from all over banded together to seal the blighted within the ruins. They planted a barrier of Radiant Trees around the city, whose divine-infused wood burns away the Blight. To this day, the trees grow unchecked, keeping the cursed Ruins of Spliffholm locked away.
Aftermath
Reeling from the horrors they witnessed in Spliffholm, veterans of the Nevercough Tribunal military forces, and its allies vowed to make sure that they would not suffer the same fate as Spliffholm, and used the incident to scapegoat the indigenous people due to their heretical ways, and opposition of The Faith of the Sacred Flame. They decided to unite all the settlements of the alliance, and form a city state named Stickyickistan. This decision was not unanimous, but was a democratic majority. All the original settlement cities eventually grew into one another finally making them indistinguishable. There are still many that identify more with the region of the city state they are from than the city state itself. Mostly the dwarves of Bongstad since that area remains the most racially homogenous of them all.

Zahur-Entertainment-Network/League-of-La.title: League of Labyrinthia
Zahur-Entertainment-Network/League-of-La.content:
“Welcome, mortals and immortals alike, to the greatest spectacle across space, time, and dimensions!”

A master entertainer and a bit of a sadistic showman, Zahur al-Nasira invites (sometimes by force) contestants from across the multiverse to compete in high-stakes challenges unlike any other. Participants ranging from bumbling fools to hardened adventurers are sent into his infinitely evolving labyrinthine dungeon of stairs constructed entirely within Zahur’s personal extra-dimensional domain. Adventurers that end up here are sorted into parties at random and each party is assigned a mysterious Patron who leads them on their fated staircase to a door. The party does not choose the staircase, rather it chooses them. The correct staircases to reach their destination simply fly into place as the Patron walks forward ahead of them to the door. When the staircases reach a threshold, their Patron will begin the ritual to open the door which involves a verbal component where the Patron begins speaking in an esoteric language only known to them and the gods, and a somatic component of a weaving or tugging motion on the literal strands of the Weave itself.

The rules are simple: survive, overcome, and profit, or perish in spectacular fashion. Each staircase in the labyrinth holds the promise of gold and glory or an untimely demise. The harder the quest, the greater the payout, and the higher the ratings. Zahur brings viewers from all over the multiverse to come watch the spectacles, but a dimension door called the Labyrinthian Link can be found in Stickyickistan on Nevercough Island downtown. Citizens can buy tickets for the events and pass through the portal to watch the show. The show can also be watched on magitech screens where they are available for purchase.
Zahur’s Entertainment Network (ZEN)
features many shows such as;

League of Labyrinthia

The original game show that made Zahur even more rich than he already was where hardened adventurer’s, criminals, and creatures of all kinds are pitted against one another.


The Wretched Chronicles

A spinoff of LoL following the adventures of an infamous warlock named Wretch who survived the game show as punishment for a heinous crime.


A.S.S.C.U.N.T

An original late night action / comedy series following a ragtag team of 4 outlaw monster hunters from Stickyickistan. This show is popular due to it’s star studded cast ;)




Just to name a few.
A League of Our Own
This is basically my creative description of how a DM takes the players of the game on a journey, but specifically for an Adventurer’s League setting. Each session is standalone and meant to be kept to an hour or two (maybe 3 let’s be real I wanna play DnD). Sessions are like episodes of a show, and don’t always feature all the same characters. These episodes may be one offs like a movie, or part of a series. These series of adventures share settings, plot points, or NPCs with official modules and are referred to as “seasons.” They feature storylines adjacent to the main plot found in published modules and are optimized for Adventurers League play. Characters will not always be the same level, DMs must follow RAW as close as possible, and characters must start at level 1. Refer to A League of Our Own for more information.

Zahur-Entertainment-Network/Zahur-al-Nas.title: Zahur al-Nasira
Zahur-Entertainment-Network/Zahur-al-Nas.content:
A being of tempestuous laughter and boundless charisma, Zahur al-Nasira is more than just a Djinni Prince. He is the Master of Mayhem, the Architect of Anarchy, and the Undisputed Host of the most exhilarating game show in all the multiverse: The League of Labyrinthia!
This one of my (Chase) DM alter egos. I like to imagine I become Zahur when I am behind the  screen. A true chaotic neutral, his domain exists within the plane of Limbo. A magnificent palace of marble, golden, and lapis lazuli held together by Zahur’s will over the chaotic nature of Limbo. He is originally from the inner Elemental Plane of Air.

Appearance & Attire
Zahur’s form is as mutable as the winds. His body shimmers between solid and ethereal, his deep blue skin streaked with arcs of crackling lightning. His robes, woven from storm clouds and embroidered with golden filigree, billow even when there is no breeze. A crown of swirling mist and gemstones sits atop his head, and his piercing silver eyes gleam with mischief and wisdom.

index.title: Welcome to Stickyickistan
index.content:
WARNING FOR PLAYERS
I am somewhat trusting you to not meta-game you little rat fucks. There will be information in here that characters do not have. I want to make the world building collaborative, so please use this for reference when creating characters for the setting, and send me your ideas/suggestions for additions/amendments to the world on discord.
Setting & Sources
Stickyickistan is my evolving homebrewed D&D world, a melting pot of various settings and sources blended into one. Intentional ambiguity allows the world to function as an open sandbox, giving both my players and me, as the DM, the freedom to explore limitless possibilities without rigid constraints. I am also lazy.
This world draws inspiration from multiple established settings, including the Forgotten Realms, Eberron, Ravnica, Dragonlance, Spelljammer, and Drakkenheim.  I am also heavily using the book Heliana’s Guide to Monster Hunting which adds systems for tracking, harvesting, crafting items from, and cooking meals made of monsters. I am trying to weave together elements of medieval fantasy, cyberpunk, and steampunk, creating an often chaotic world where magic, technology, and intrigue collide, sometimes in ways that defy logic, but that’s part of the fun.
Welcome to Stickyickistan
At the heart of the setting lies the sprawling metropolis of Stickyickistan. Stickyickistan is an island on the planet of Mythmos that is enshrouded in magic, and has one of the largest economies of all the realms. Their economy is based on the cultivation, and export of a wondrous magical plant called Arcannabis. The size of the island and how far away it is from other land masses is mysterious at best. Even the most sophisticated magic and technology isn’t capable of measuring distance within a certain distance of the island. This area is a Bermuda Triangle like place where pilots, and sailors have reported extreme magical weather events, and terrifying creatures from above and below. The presence of such large amounts of Arcanite beneath Mount Zooka has warped the fabric of time, space, and the weave itself around the island which is what causes these phenomenon. This makes it incredibly hard to produce a map of the whole island, as the coastlines are enigmatic at best. It can be seen from the Lumytholarispace however, so it does appear on maps of Mythos, but appears much smaller than going there would lead you to believe.
Planet of Mythmos
Mythmos is an oblate sphere of rock and water with an Arcanite core that orbits a fiery sun called Lumytholaris (loo-mi-tho-law-ris). It has one moon, and a few other celestial neighbours in Lumytholarispace, but they are all largely uninhabited. Most trips outside the mythic atmosphere of Mythmos are mining expeditions for rare cosmic elements. Trace amounts of Arcanite and Delerium can be found in the solar system’s asteroid belt. Sages from across the realms have put forth differing theories to explain the order of the cosmos throughout history. These included bizarre concepts such as the “great wheel”, the “world axis”, the “conjunction of the spheres”, “planetary orbits”, and “general relativity”. There is no consensus; every theorist is quick to point out the glaring flaws and logical inconsistencies in competing hypotheses.
